theory.intro: A **credit card** is a reducing balance loan: interest is calculated on the amount currently owing, and repayments are subtracted from that balance. Use the card conditions stated in the question, including its interest rate, interest-free conditions and day-counting rule.
facts: The daily interest rate is the annual rate divided by $365$: $18.25\%$ p.a. gives $r = \dfrac{0.1825}{365}$.
Each purchase is its own compound interest calculation, $FV = PV(1+r)^{n}$, where $n$ is that purchase's own number of days.
Count the days as the question directs: from $8$ March to $31$ March inclusive is $31 - 8 + 1 = 24$ days.

With no opening debt, repayments or fees, the **closing balance** is the sum of the amounts owing on each purchase at the statement date. Include any other amounts or repayments as directed by the question.
With no repayments or fees, interest charged on the purchases is the closing balance minus their original total.
Follow the stated **interest-free period** conditions. A question may say that it applies only when the previous statement was paid in full; a minimum payment would not meet that condition.
The **minimum payment** is a small percentage of the closing balance, not the whole balance, so a debt repaid that way lasts a long time.
A **cash advance** is cash taken out on the card. It may have a different rate and different interest-free conditions from purchases; use the terms given.
Keep the full value in the calculator and round the money answer once, at the end.
steps: Write down the daily interest rate.
Count the number of days for each purchase.
Combine the required amounts, subtract repayments at the stated time, and round the money answer at the end. Find interest or the minimum payment if asked.

workedExamples.question_text: A $\$270$ cash advance has no interest-free period and is charged $18.25\%$ p.a. compounded daily. It is taken on $19$ May; interest includes that date and the statement date of $31$ May. Find (a) the daily rate as a decimal, (b) the number of charged days and (c) the amount owing to the nearest cent.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $r=0.1825\div365=0.0005$.
(b) $n=31-19+1=13$ days. Include both dates.
(c) $FV=270(1.0005)^{13}\approx\$271.76$. The advance conditions say that interest applies for all these days.

workedExamples.question_text: A card has no interest-free period and charges $14.6\%$ p.a. compounded daily, including purchase and statement dates. The only purchases are $\$350$ on $8$ April and $\$120$ on $23$ April; the statement date is $30$ April. There is no opening balance, repayment or fee. Find (a) the closing balance, (b) the interest charged and (c) a minimum payment of $2.5\%$ of the closing balance. Give money answers to the nearest cent.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$r=0.146\div365=0.0004$.
The purchases accrue interest for $30-8+1=23$ days and $30-23+1=8$ days.
(a) Closing balance $=350(1.0004)^{23}+120(1.0004)^8\approx\$473.62$. Keep both calculator values unrounded when adding.
(b) Interest $=350(1.0004)^{23}+120(1.0004)^8-470\approx\$3.62$.
(c) Minimum payment $=0.025(473.62)\approx\$11.84$. It is a payment towards the balance, not the interest charge.

workedExamples.question_text:
A card charges $21.9\%$ p.a. compounded daily and a borrower owes $\$1100$. No other purchases or fees occur. Compare the following repayments of $\$450$.
(a) Interest is charged for $18$ days, then the repayment is made.
(b) The repayment is made first, then interest is charged on the balance left for $18$ days. Find both final balances to the nearest cent.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$r=0.219\div365=0.0006$.
(a) Grow the debt, then subtract the repayment:
$1100(1.0006)^{18}-450\approx\$661.94$.
(b) Subtract first, then grow the balance left:
$(1100-450)(1.0006)^{18}\approx\$657.06$. The timing changes which amount attracts interest.

workedExamples.question_text: A card requires a minimum payment of $5\%$ of its statement closing balance or $\$25$, whichever is greater. Find the payment for (a) a $\$340$ balance and (b) a $\$980$ balance.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $0.05(340)=\$17$. The fixed minimum of $\$25$ is greater, so pay $\$25$.
(b) $0.05(980)=\$49$, greater than $\$25$, so pay $\$49$.

workedExamples.question_text:
A card's stated conditions allow $55$ interest-free days only if the previous statement was paid in full. A $\$320$ purchase is paid off after $20$ days.
(a) Find the interest when the previous statement was paid in full.
(b) Find the interest if the previous statement was not paid in full and interest is charged for all $20$ days at $14.6\%$ p.a., compounded daily.
(c) Explain why this card is a reducing balance loan.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The stated conditions are met and $20<55$, so the interest is $\$0$.
(b) The interest-free condition is not met.
Interest $=320(1.0004)^{20}-320\approx\$2.57$.
(c) Interest is calculated on the amount currently owing. A repayment is subtracted from that amount, so future interest uses the balance left. The conditions, not just the number of days, determine whether interest applies.

workedExamples.question_text: A purchase of $\$1500$ grows to $\$1509.03$ after $15$ charged days of daily compounding. The annual rate is one of $10.95\%$, $14.6\%$, $18.25\%$ or $21.9\%$. Find it by testing the four rates.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Use $FV=1500\left(1+\dfrac{\text{annual decimal rate}}{365}\right)^{15}$.
$10.95\%$ gives $\$1506.76$; $14.6\%$ gives $\$1509.03$; $18.25\%$ gives $\$1511.29$; $21.9\%$ gives $\$1513.56$, all to the nearest cent.
The rate is $14.6\%$ p.a. Testing uses the same daily-compounding calculation each time.

foundation.question_text:
A credit card charges interest at $21.9\%$ p.a. compounded daily.
Find the daily interest rate, as a fraction and as a decimal.

A purchase is made on $14$ May and the statement is issued on $31$ May.
Interest is charged from and including the purchase date up to and including the statement date.
For how many days is interest charged?

A purchase of $\$640$ is made on a credit card with no interest-free period, charging $16.4\%$ p.a. compounded daily.
Interest is charged for $25$ days.
Find the amount owing, to the nearest cent.

A purchase of $\$1250$ is made on a credit card with no interest-free period, charging $14.6\%$ p.a. compounded daily.
Interest is charged for $30$ days.
Find the interest charged, to the nearest cent.

A credit card charges $14.6\%$ p.a. compounded daily with no interest-free period, from and including the purchase date to and including the statement date of $30$ April.
A purchase of $\$460$ is made on $22$ April and one of $\$180$ on $27$ April.
Find the closing balance, to the nearest cent.
foundation.solution_text:
$r = \dfrac{0.146}{365}$
$\$460$ purchase: $n = 30 - 22 + 1 = 9$ days
$FV = 460\left(1 + \dfrac{0.146}{365}\right)^{9} = \$461.66$
$\$180$ purchase: $n = 30 - 27 + 1 = 4$ days
$FV = 180\left(1 + \dfrac{0.146}{365}\right)^{4} = \$180.29$
Closing balance $=460(1.0004)^9+180(1.0004)^4\approx\$641.95$. Use unrounded purchase values when adding.

foundation.question_text:
A credit card statement shows a closing balance of $\$2480.60$.
The minimum payment is $2\%$ of the closing balance, or $\$30$, whichever is greater.
Find the minimum payment.
foundation.solution_text:
$2\%$ of the closing balance $= 0.02 \times 2480.60$
$= \$49.61$
Since $\$49.61 > \$30$, the minimum payment is $\$49.61$.

foundation.question_text:
Mia's credit card has a $55$-day interest-free period, which applies only when the previous statement was paid in full.
Mia paid her previous statement in full, then bought a television for $\$780$ and paid the new statement in full $40$ days later.
How much interest is she charged on the purchase?
foundation.solution_text:
The previous statement was paid in full, so the interest-free period applies.
The $\$780$ was repaid after $40$ days, which is inside the $55$-day interest-free period.
No interest is charged, so the interest is $\$0$.

foundation.question_text: Explain why a credit card is an example of a reducing balance loan, and state one way in which it is different from a home loan.
foundation.solution_text:
Interest on a credit card is calculated on the amount currently owing, not always on the amount first spent. A repayment reduces that amount; subsequent interest uses the remaining balance.
A home-loan question commonly specifies a fixed repayment, while a credit card may specify only a minimum payment and allow the cardholder to repay more.

development.question_text:
A credit card charges $18.25\%$ p.a. compounded daily with no interest-free period, from and including the purchase date to and including the statement date of $31$ March.
A purchase of $\$840$ is made on $8$ March and one of $\$250$ on $19$ March.
Find the closing balance and the interest charged, to the nearest cent.

Jonah owes $\$900$ on a credit card charging $14.6\%$ p.a. compounded daily.
Interest is charged for $20$ days, after which he repays $\$400$.
How much does he owe immediately after the repayment, to the nearest cent?

Rosa owes $\$1600$ on a credit card charging $21.9\%$ p.a. compounded daily.
Interest is charged for $12$ days, after which she repays $\$650$.
How much does she owe immediately after the repayment, to the nearest cent?

A cash advance of $\$500$ is taken on a credit card at $25.55\%$ p.a. compounded daily. The card has no interest-free period for cash advances.
Interest is charged for $40$ days. Find the amount owing at the end of those $40$ days, to the nearest cent.

A credit card charges $21.9\%$ p.a. compounded daily with no interest-free period, from and including the purchase date to and including the statement date of $30$ June.
The June transactions are shown.
$\begin{array}{|l|l|r|}\hline \textbf{Date} & \textbf{Transaction} & \textbf{Amount} \\ \hline \text{6 June} & \text{Airline tickets} & \$500 \\ \hline \text{18 June} & \text{Car service} & \$300 \\ \hline \end{array}$
Find the interest charged for June, to the nearest cent.

Dev's credit card has a $55$-day interest-free period that applies only when the previous statement was paid in full.
Last month Dev paid only the minimum, so no interest-free period applies.
He makes a purchase of $\$620$ and interest at $18.25\%$ p.a. compounded daily is charged for $22$ days.
Find the interest charged, to the nearest cent.
development.solution_text:
The previous statement was not paid in full, so interest runs from the purchase date.
$r = \dfrac{0.1825}{365} = 0.0005$, $n = 22$
$FV = 620(1.0005)^{22}$
$= \$626.86$
Interest $= 626.86 - 620$
$= \$6.86$

mastery.question_text:
A credit card charges $21.9\%$ p.a. compounded daily with no interest-free period, from and including the purchase date to and including the statement date of $31$ August.
The August transactions are shown.
$\begin{array}{|l|l|r|}\hline \textbf{Date} & \textbf{Transaction} & \textbf{Amount} \\ \hline \text{5 August} & \text{Furniture} & \$700 \\ \hline \text{17 August} & \text{Tyres} & \$400 \\ \hline \text{26 August} & \text{Groceries} & \$250 \\ \hline \end{array}$
The minimum payment is $3\%$ of the closing balance.
Find the closing balance, the interest charged and the minimum payment, each to the nearest cent.

A single purchase of $\$2000$ on a credit card compounding daily grew to $\$2012.03$ over $20$ days, with interest charged for all $20$ days.
The annual rate is one of $10.95\%$, $14.6\%$, $18.25\%$ or $21.9\%$.
Find the annual interest rate.
mastery.solution_text:
Test all four annual rates in $FV=2000\left(1+\dfrac{\text{annual decimal rate}}{365}\right)^{20}$.
$10.95\%$: $r=0.0003$, $FV\approx\$2012.03$.
$14.6\%$: $r=0.0004$, $FV\approx\$2016.06$.
$18.25\%$: $r=0.0005$, $FV\approx\$2020.10$.
$21.9\%$: $r=0.0006$, $FV\approx\$2024.14$.
Only $10.95\%$ p.a. gives the stated balance to the nearest cent.

mastery.question_text:
Priya's credit card statement shows a closing balance of $\$3200$, and the minimum payment is $2.5\%$ of the closing balance.
She pays only the minimum on $1$ October and makes no further purchases.
Interest at $21.9\%$ p.a. compounded daily is charged on the amount owing for the $31$ days of October.
How much does she owe at the end of October, to the nearest cent?
